topics.topic: Behavior when activating a flow version that is already active (new FlowActivation record vs no-op/return existing)
questions: If the owner/agent asks to activate the same flow version that is already active, does the kernel create a new FlowActivation record or return the existing active state unchanged?
When activate is called for the version that is already active, does the kernel create a new FlowActivation record or return the existing active state without change?

quotes:
A flow's active version is the one recorded
last (K-17); a new activation replaces the previous one at once, and runs already
started keep the version they pinned.
judgement.why: This topic is about unchanged M18 text, and the listed changes did not touch flow-activation idempotence or make it newly material.

topics.topic: Run status precedence when execution immediately or simultaneously encounters waiting conditions
questions: When a run starts and its first executable node(s) immediately require owner approval or hit unreachable service, is the initial persisted status `running` first, or directly `awaiting_approval`/`pending`?
What single run `status` must be stored when some branches are still executing and at least one waiting point exists?

quotes: While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running (K-09).
judgement.why: This question targets unchanged run-status wording, and the reopen diff does not change run lifecycle semantics.

topics.topic: What binding/model-read behavior is allowed when a service has no selected instance
questions: If no instance is selected for a service, does ManifestOperation exist without `base_url`, or is reading/proposing/accepting bindings for that service refused at model-read time?
Are `propose binding` and `accept binding` allowed for a service that currently has no selected instance?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A: the kernel allows ManifestOperation reading and allows proposing/accepting a binding even when no service instance is selected, and only refuses later invocation as not invocable; Behavior B: the kernel refuses ManifestOperation reading/propose/accept for that service until an instance is selected. The agent notices on propose, and the owner notices on accept.
judgement.why: The texts say a service with no selected instance is not invocable, but do not close whether binding proposal/acceptance is still allowed in that condition.

topics.topic: Whether every service must have a selected instance in installation.service_instances (mandatory vs optional)
questions: Must an installation select exactly one instance for every service, or may some services have no selected instance?
Is selecting an instance mandatory for every service, or may a service have no selected instance?

quotes:
An installation selects one manifest instance per service; no flow, run or agent
chooses another.
a service with none selected is not invocable
judgement.why: State 0 requires one selected instance per service, while State 1 explicitly allows none for a service.

topics.topic: Authority required for retrying a draft-write after a not_applied result
questions: If a `draft-write` attempt is resolved `not_applied` and retried, must that retry obtain a per-attempt owner approval, or still run only under flow activation authority?

topics.topic: ManifestOperation identity/lifecycle when selected instance address or headers change
questions: If selected instance address/headers change without changing the operation record digest, is that a new ManifestOperation fact for lifecycle/reads, or the same one?

topics.topic: Run terminal-state rule when failures coexist with unresolved waiting points
questions: If a run has a failed node and also unresolved waiting points, when does it become final `failed` versus remain waiting for owner actions?

topics.topic: Whether a proven read-only flow version auto-activates or requires an explicit activate action
questions: For a proven read-only flow version, is activation automatic immediately after proof, or only when someone calls the activate action?

topics.topic: Which action reads SpooledFile bytes and whether it is in State 0 scope
questions: Which product action reads spooled file bytes, and is it part of the State 0 surface or a later addition?
